settings.prompt:
Autonomously review this Java source repository for potential security
vulnerabilities using the available read-only tools. Do not ask the user questions or summarize
tool output. Copy exact relative paths from list_files or index results; never invent or prefix a path.
A file listing or index hint is only navigation; inspect original source and seek
counter-evidence before deciding. Trace plausible untrusted input to security-sensitive
operations where possible, and check relevant guards and configuration. Report at most 10
candidates supported by exact source lines, with root cause, preconditions, counter-evidence,
and missing evidence. Do not assume a vulnerability exists. If source review finds no supported
candidate, submit an empty candidate list. Your final action must be submit_findings; natural
language commentary is not a report. Do not use project names, dataset identifiers, or a guessed
known answer as evidence.

counter_evidence: SecurityMemberAccess implements exclusion by class, by package name list, and by package name patterns, plus a properties accept/deny Map
isAccessible enforces the preCheck result and the exclusions before permitting member access
Static method access and eval expressions are off unless explicitly enabled in configuration
candidates.description: SecurityMemberAccess gates access to static methods behind an allowStaticMethodAccess flag that is injected via setAllowStaticMethodAccess (wired to XWorkConstants.ALLOW_STATIC_METHOD_ACCESS in the read span). OgnlUtil similarly exposes setAllowStaticMethodAccess and setEnableEvalExpression. When an application enables static method access (or eval expressions), OGNL expressions that reach the value/eval path can invoke static members. The read code does contain defensive allow/deny logic: an excluded-classes set, excluded package name patterns, a Map of excludedProperties/acceptProperties, and a preCheck/handler gate on isAccessible. That design is counter-evidence against trivial OGNL injection. If the exclusion sets are left empty or misconfigured while static access is enabled, the effective protection is reduced. In the read spans I did not find a concrete request-parameter-to-eval data flow, so this remains a configuration-sensitive candidate rather than a confirmed vulnerability.
missing_evidence: No traced data flow from a request parameter to an OGNL evaluation sink within the read spans
Default values of excludedClasses/excludedPackageNames/excludedPackageNamePatterns (default.properties) were not read
Whether/how any framework endpoint passes request-influenced expressions to setValue/getValue was not verified
preconditions: Application sets the allow-static-method-access XWork constant to true (or calls OgnlUtil.setAllowStaticMethodAccess(true))
Excluded classes / excluded package names / patterns sets are empty or too narrow for the deployment
An OGNL expression influenced by request input reaches an OGNL setValue/getValue/eval path
candidates.title: Static-method access in OGNL evaluation is configurable and not default-denied by code read here (SecurityMemberAccess/OgnlUtil)

counter_evidence: Resource lookup is classpath-scoped, limiting filesystem exposure
Path cleaning and prefix handling are applied before lookup
candidates.description: DefaultStaticContentLoader.findStaticResource cleanPath logic cleans the requested path and buildPath reconstructs the resource path, which is then URL-decoded. The cleanup uses substring(7) (assuming a fixed known prefix length) and the loader can be configured with a manual path. A manually-set/cleaned path could retain traversal-like segments; the resulting resource is then checked with resourceUrl.getFile().endsWith(pathEnding) before being opened, and a resource that does not match the expected ending returns not-found. Resource resolution goes through a classpath-based lookup, which limits exposure compared with arbitrary filesystem access. The endsWith guard and classpath scoping are counter-evidence, so no file disclosure is claimed; the substring(7) assumption and the decode-after-reconstruction step are reported as a low-confidence candidate because unusual or unexpected path inputs could be mis-cleaned.
missing_evidence: No traced request showing a cleaned path that both escapes the intended package and passes the endsWith guard
Behavior of URLDecoder on the reconstructed path with encoded traversal sequences was not executed or verified
The exact guard/cleaning line ranges within findStaticResource were not fully re-read line-by-line in this session
preconditions: serveStatic / static content loading enabled and a request path routed to DefaultStaticContentLoader
A path value whose cleaned form still resolves to an unintended resource yet satisfies the endsWith(pathEnding) guard
candidates.title: DefaultStaticContentLoader path cleaning uses fixed-length substring(7) and post-decode path reconstruction
